s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of focal neurological deficits with evidence of cerebral infarction
key_facts: 25-year-old woman
Presented to emergency department with acute neurological symptoms
Similar event 3 years prior requiring mechanical thrombectomy
History of well-controlled hypertension, obesity, migraines, and recurrent immune thrombocytopenia
Current medications: aspirin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin
History of tobacco use, stopped after first event
Family history of similar condition in older sister
Vital signs: Temperature 37.6°C, respiratory rate 14, heart rate 78 beats/min, blood pressure 179/98 mm Hg
Neurologic examination revealed left gaze preference, right facial droop, right upper- and lower-extremity weakness
Initial National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score was 22
Laboratory tests showed elevated leukocytes, low hemoglobin, and low platelet count
Imaging studies showed left MCA M1 occlusion and left MCA-distribution infarction

shortlist.label: Cardioembolic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of similar event requiring mechanical thrombectomy and current presentation of acute onset of focal neurological deficits with evidence of cerebral infarction

shortlist.label: Moyamoya disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age, presentation, and lack of clear atherosclerotic risk factors make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Central nervous system vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's recurrent events and lack of clear atherosclerotic risk factors make this a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of recurrent immune thrombocytopenia and current presentation of stroke make this a possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's recurrent strokes at a young age, family history of a similar condition, and lack of traditional cardiovascular risk factors suggest a non-atherosclerotic cause, with Moyamoya disease being a strong candidate given its tendency to cause strokes in young adults and its familial occurrence

rejected.label: Cardioembolic stroke
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of traditional cardiovascular risk factors make this less likely

rejected.label: Central nervous system vasculitis
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of inflammation or vasculitis on laboratory tests or imaging studies

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's history of recurrent immune thrombocytopenia could suggest an autoimmune disorder, but the lack of other specific criteria for antiphospholipid syndrome makes this less likely

rejected.label: Takayasu arteritis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and imaging studies do not suggest large vessel vasculitis, which is characteristic of Takayasu arteritis
